parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity or same-sex conduct, and no documented border or document-mismatch exposure for visitors; entry axis is largely clear. The worst documented features are custody placement by birth sex (ordinary male dormitories, mandatory head-shaving, safety dependent on inmate hierarchies, a segregated annex elsewhere) and scattered anti-trans violence — two 2025 killings, a rape, an on-stage assault — with no per-capita rate and no state-implicated pattern, though the human-rights commission names a 'disturbing pattern of transfemicide'. No national anti-discrimination law and no legal gender recognition exist; protection is a local patchwork. Two local cross-dressing ordinances with imprisonment penalties are on the books but enforcement is undocumented. Civil society is active and functioning, which keeps outcomes from being catastrophic but leaves recourse thin.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented; no border or document-mismatch friction reported for visitors.
entry_documents.protection: No criminalisation of trans identity; no documented entry refusals.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passport governs; absence of domestic LGR does not reach visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans women held in male dormitories, mandatory head-shaving, safety via inmate hierarchies; 'survival weddings' as protection strategy; annex batching elsewhere.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: One jail relocates LGBT detainees to an annex 'to prevent abuse'; practice varies and is unsourced generally.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An arrest for any reason places a visitor in birth-sex custody with no national placement rule.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Local ordinances in two localities ban cross-dressing/female attire, one under imprisonment penalty; enforcement not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Nine provinces and 32+ municipalities prohibit SOGI discrimination; school uniform and gender-responsive education policies.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor's protection depends on locality; refusals of service by establishments documented with little consequence.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors; no care-denial cases in the record.
care_services.protection: HIV-status/SOGI anti-discrimination statute; right-to-care card in one major city for medical decisions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police arrested 20 peaceful Pride participants in 2020 and prosecuted under assembly and disease statutes; 'grave scandal' provision available for public conduct; violence in custody delegated to inmate hierarchies.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Human-rights commission investigates but lacks enforcement power; no documented police extortion or sweeps.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Pride attendance carries documented arrest risk for a visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Family/honour harm (conversion therapy by a religious group) is resident-sphere, not documented reaching visitors.
minors_guardians.protection: Anti-bullying rules and school uniform policy include SOGI; no visitor-specific minor exposure documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two trans women killed on the same day in 2025; a 2025 rape of a trans woman; a drag performer assaulted; killings reported since 2012; post-siege harassment of perceived-LGBT people; commission calls it a 'disturbing pattern'.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Rape arrest made; mayor's public apology after stage assault; no state implication or impunity pattern documented; no denominator so rate unknown.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Scattered societal violence, thin national remedy; local ordinances vary.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No national SOGI anti-discrimination law after 25 years; government rejected the equality bill in 2022; no legal gender recognition; 'good moral character' discretion.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active civil society, trans legislator, 2023 executive-order LGBTQIA+ affairs committee, local statutes with fines/jail for SOGIE harassment.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is locality-dependent; national remedy effectively absent.

anchor_checks.comparison: Less universal exposure than 0.45-D's nightly hotel-database registration: no documented visitor registration or border disclosure here. But this dossier's custody-by-birth-sex with documented harm structure and killing pattern is comparable severity; net slightly above 0.45-D.

Comparable scattered harassment and service refusal with uneven remedies; but 0.55-E's worst feature is ejection and humiliation, whereas here documented custodial placement by birth sex with head-shaving and a killing pattern the commission calls a pattern sit heavier — this case sits below 0.55-E.

Well below 0.75-C: there, detention is brief, remedies (tribunal, compensation) work, and no killing pattern exists. Here remedies are thin at national level, custody placement is unsafe by default, and transfemicide is flagged — a full band lower.

Above 0.25-B: no police extortion/shakedown pattern, no systemic custodial abuse campaign; violence is scattered with some functioning response (arrest, apology), and entry is clear — the exposures are narrower in reach.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is decentralised: no national anti-discrimination statute, no legal gender recognition, and a 25-year-stalled equality bill mean a visitor's protection depends entirely on locality. Entry and daily life present no documented universal-exposure measure — the visitor can often move without disclosure. The dominant exposures are (1) custody by birth sex with degraded safety, reachable through any arrest including the documented 2020 Pride arrests, and (2) scattered societal violence — killings, rape, assault — without a national remedy and without a published rate, so severity is real but frequency is unestablished. Local cross-dressing ordinances with imprisonment penalties exist but enforcement is undocumented. Active civil society and partial local protections keep this above the High Risk band; the unsafe default custody placement and thin national recourse hold it mid-Elevated, around 0.50.
